$comment: 🖱️ A wheel is applied at the point ITS OWN events carried, never at wherever the pointer has since moved. `🎮️wgpu-browser-input-wire/🔣️.json` already pins that a DOM wheel's position survives both hops into `DispatchEvent::Scroll { x, y, delta_x, delta_y }`; this oracle pins the hop AFTER it — what the frame does with that position. The wgpu tick is input-driven, so a wheel is normally drained by a LATER event, and the frame's scene-surface gate plus `World3dState::bounds.contains` both answer for whatever point it applies at.

rule.statement: Every wheel notch is applied at its own point. Consecutive notches coalesce their deltas only while the point does not move; a notch at a NEW point opens a new pending application, and a frame drains the pending applications oldest first. A pointer event moves the pointer and never a pending notch. Draining leaves none, a notch whose deltas cancel applies nothing, and a stream longer than the pending capacity coalesces into its newest application rather than growing.

cases.name: one-notch-applies-at-its-own-point
cases.why: The baseline: a single wheel over the preview centre.

cases.name: a-later-pointer-move-does-not-move-the-pending-wheel
cases.why: The first defect of this family, verbatim. The probe wheels over the preview centre and then nudges the pointer to the top-left corner to make the input-driven tick run. Measured on 6118 before the fix: `wheel gate x=5 y=5 delta=-480 hit=None control=None propagates=true worlds=[("procedural-preview", false)]` — four notches applied 1200 px away from where the user scrolled, so the World3d authority saw `wheel=0` on every one of its 335 intents and the camera was byte-identical before and after (📓️wgpu-end-to-end-verification-2026-09-14.md §5.1).

cases.name: notches-at-two-points-are-two-applications
cases.why: The RESIDUAL defect this oracle was widened for, verbatim from the battery's own `world3d-editor / h7_wheel_zoom`. The probe scrolls once over the preview centre and then nudges the pointer 1 px into the top-left corner between notches, so the browser's wheel stream genuinely carries five points. Keeping only the NEWEST point coalesced all five into one application in the corner: measured on 6118 (2026-09-14 15:30 battery), five `Scroll { x: 1208, y: 461 }` … `{ x: 6, y: 6 }` events produced `wheel=0` on all 337 world3d intents and the camera stayed `[4,-4,3]->[0,0,0]/45deg` while hover answered `Some("extrude@solid")`. A notch over the geometry and a notch in the corner are not one gesture.

cases.name: a-travelling-wheel-stream-applies-each-point-once
cases.why: Trackpad momentum under a moving cursor. Each point is its own zoom anchor, so the stream is two applications and not one at the end of the travel.

cases.name: a-stationary-burst-is-one-application
cases.why: The common case a reader must not pay per notch for: a user holding the pointer still over the preview and spinning the wheel. The point never moves, so the whole burst coalesces into ONE application at that point.

cases.name: taking-the-wheel-leaves-none
cases.why: A second frame with no new scroll applies nothing — the accumulator is not a level, it is a pending delta.

cases.name: opposite-notches-cancel-and-apply-nothing
cases.why: Zero delta is not a wheel. The frame must fall through without gating a surface or publishing a camera verb.

cases.name: pointer-events-alone-apply-nothing
cases.why: Moving the pointer must never invent a wheel.

cases.name: a-stream-longer-than-the-capacity-coalesces-into-its-newest-application
cases.why: Fixed credits: nine notches at nine distinct points may not grow an unbounded queue inside a frame. The first eight keep their own points and the ninth merges into the eighth, which then carries the newest point — the same tail rule the pre-fix accumulator applied to the whole stream.
